issue_context.title: [Feature/Bug] Firefox: Unable to override "dom.push.serverURL" in a persistent context
issue_context.body:
Hi!
This is a bit of a mixed issue, depending on the solution you might consider it a feature request or a bug.

My use case: Testing service worker push notifications. I had this working in puppeteer for a year and I'm migrating to playwright. I know that it's a bit of a tricky use case, but it works well enough for our use case and is certainly much better than no test at all.

On Chrome, I had to setup a persistent context as the Push API isn't available in incognito, that's alright. I extended `test` to change the browser context, generating a new user data dir on each run, it all works fine.

The issue is that on Firefox, I need to change some user prefs (notable "dom.push.serverURL", as Playwright sets it to empty). On a non persistent context, it's easy: `launchOptions: { firefoxUserPrefs: { "dom.push.serverURL": "wss://push.services.mozilla.com/" } }` works. It's a bit of a shame that I have to hardcode this value, but it's fine.

For maintainablity reasons I do not with to use a standard context on one browser and a persistent on another one. But as you know, there are no "firefoxUserPrefs" on a persistent context: the recommended approach is to set a `user.js`.

I did it so I get `user_pref("dom.push.serverURL", "etc....");` in `user.js`, but this setting is overwritten by the builtin playwright autoconfig. I could not get it to work on a persistent context.

I also tried opening Firefox once to generate the persistent profile, closing it and editing "prefs.js" before restarting it but autoconfig overwrites everything back to the default values.

Ultimately I got it working by launching firefox in a standard way, and chrome starts in a persistent context. Not ideal but does the job for now.

So the feature request would be: Can we get `firefoxUserPrefs` in persistent contexts?
and the bug would be: I can't override "dom.push.serverURL" in a persistent context by manipulating the user data directory


I see multiple ways to address this:

- Maybe setting https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/fe7847b126ce2059d02fbbbc1f632b04fdae3ef7/browser_patches/firefox/preferences/playwright.cfg#L111 to `defaultPref` would allow me to override it for good in `user.js`. I could not test this.
- Modifying "playwright-core/lib/server/firefox/ffBrowser.js" to pass the userPrefs even on a persistent context works fine: I wonder why it is that way, maybe because there was not a valid use case to justify a public API yet? I understand the wish to keep a public API as minimalistic/clean as you can.
- Adding a native setting to enable push API. Sounds like a lot of work for a niche case.


Ideally I would like a way to revert Firefox user prefs to their default value without hardcoding them.

Thanks in advance,
